summary: This graph centres on two recent confidence-aware reranking ideas for RAG: LLM-Confidence Reranker (LCR), which derives a black-box confidence signal from Maximum Semantic Cluster Proportion (MSCP) and reranks candidates in a training-free way, and CAR, which uses generator-side confidence change to do query-guided, uncertainty-aware reranking. Both are evaluated mainly on BEIR-style retrieval benchmarks, with LCR also using TREC, and both report NDCG@5 improvements; CAR additionally links ranking gains to downstream generation F1. The graph also includes the main LLM reranking baselines and surrounding concepts that shape the landscape: listwise reranking methods such as RankGPT, RankZephyr, and FIRST; fine-grained pointwise scoring such as Beyond Yes and No; classic learning-to-rank methods like RankT5; and strong cross-encoder baselines like BGE-Reranker-Large and GTE-7B. Evaluation infrastructure and judge-style concepts are represented by RankArena and RAGPerf.
